subject: Occupancy modeling with offset for area size

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Occupancy modeling with offset for area size
parts:
Dear unmarkers,

 

I have a static occupancy analysis with transect units of two different lengths. My question is how to accommodate transect length in the analysis ?

 

I just read an article where they said that one could use a complementary log-log link function and treat length as a simple offset of the following kind (indices omitted):

Prob(z = 1 | covariates x) = 1 - exp(-(A * exp(alpha + beta * x)))

 

I could easily fit this model in the BUGS language, but I was wondering whether I could fit it or something similar in unmarked (without having to implement the cloglog link in the source code).

 

Thanks and kind regards -- Marc

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Occupancy modeling with offset for area size
parts:
At this point I don't think so
It would be easy to do this but our development focus is on other things right now so it will probably not get done for quite some time.
(note: look at the occu() function code and you see "plogis" used there -- make up a function called clogloginv or whatever and maybe that would be all there is too it..... I need to think about that.)

andy

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Occupancy modeling with offset for area size
parts: yea I think thats fine -- if cloglog(psi) = a + b*x  then if occupancy rates aren't too high I think logit(psi) = a + b*x is probably a close approximation, so if log(A) should be in the first model as an offset then too it should be in the 2nd I bet.

andy
